newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish share index closes at new high, more ahead.
newsitem.headline: Danish share index closes at new high, more ahead.

text.p: The Danish top-20 KFX share index closed at a new all-time record high on Friday, buoyed by a stronger dollar and positive U.S. trends, with dealers expecting more moderate gains early in the coming week.
"The new KFX index record is primarily accountable to the dollar and positive developments on Wall Street starting on Thursday which have bolstered Danish stock," one dealer said.

After a sluggish start, the KFX top-20 index closed 1.92 point higher at 136.60, beating the last all-time high record closing figure of 136.13 reached on December 30, the last day of trading in 1996.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.148 billion crowns.The KFX March future closed untraded at 135.70.

Key blue chip Novo Nordisk, reaping the benefit of the firmer dollar and the announcement that it will launch its Nordtropin human growth hormone in the United States this year, climbed five crowns to close at 537.

Otherwise Carlsberg and Sophus Berendsen, aided by the bullish pound sterling, put on four and eight crowns respectively to finish at 399 and 763, while Tele Danmark ended six crowns up at 327 on restructuring plans.
